Dai-Ichi Life to Buy Fidelity Life Assurance for Nearly $370 Million
By Kosaku Narioka
Dai-ichi Life Group has agreed to acquire New Zealand's Fidelity Life Assurance for nearly $370 million, as part of efforts to expand its international business.

The Japanese life insurer said Thursday that its wholly owned unit in New Zealand signed an agreement to buy the Auckland-based insurer for 630 million New Zealand dollars, equivalent to US$368.6 million.
Dai-ichi said the planned acquisition is expected to contribute about NZ$60 million annually to its adjusted profit.
The Japanese company aims to increase contributions from its international life-insurance business to about 50% of the group's adjusted profit by the fiscal year starting April 2030.
Dai-ichi plans to acquire shares of Fidelity Life from Guardians of New Zealand Superannuation and other shareholders.
The acquisition is expected to be completed between March and July 2027, the Japanese company said.
